edges.notes: Netfilter is a Linux kernel networking subsystem providing packet filtering hooks and related facilities per kernel documentation.
Netfilter tables and rules are scoped per network namespace on Linux.
Modifying firewall rules typically requires network administration capabilities (e.g. CAP_NET_ADMIN) per common Linux privilege model.
eBPF programs can attach in multiple kernel subsystems; netfilter is a separate hook framework for classic iptables/nftables paths.
kube-proxy and node networking on Linux commonly program netfilter rules for Services unless replaced by other datapaths.
Docker’s Linux networking modes interact with iptables/nftables rules for NAT and bridge forwarding in typical deployments.
Cilium often uses eBPF for datapath policy; clusters may still have residual netfilter rules or migrate away from iptables kube-proxy modes.
Envoy is a userspace L7 proxy; host L3/L4 policy may still be implemented with netfilter separately in layered stacks.
